source: Lu, Foldes, Lewis (2024) Memory replay in TMR and birdsong: CLS models
finding: A small complementary-learning-systems network was built to simulate TMR. A cue switches hippocampal replay from spontaneous or noise-driven mode to cue-driven mode.
numbers: Four model variants (hippocampus plastic or stable x replay spontaneous or noise-driven). 100 simulated repetitions per model. Cued pair beat non-cued pairs only in the TMR condition.
quote: TMR cues, similar to sensory cues in training, change the model's replay mechanism from a normal mode to a cue-driven mode.
limits: Idealised, abstract model. Effect sizes far larger than real human TMR because replay is perfect and the number of simulated trials is large.
agent_relevance: Shows a clean mechanism: a cue is a retrieval key that biases which stored item gets replayed. This is the closest machine analogue of TMR.

source: Lu, Foldes, Lewis (2024) CLS model: duration of the TMR effect
finding: The TMR gain lasts or grows only if the hippocampal store consolidates its own replay. If the hippocampus is stable, the TMR effect decays over time.
numbers: Table 1: the two stable models show a positive targeted effect and zero non-targeted effect; the plastic models differ from each other and from the stable ones in sign and trend.
limits: Qualitative sign table, not fitted to data. Human peaks after more than a week are cited but not reproduced.
agent_relevance: Cue-driven rehearsal helps durably only if the store being rehearsed is itself updated. For an agent: cueing a frozen note store gives a one-off boost, not lasting change.

source: Lu, Foldes, Lewis (2024) CLS model: cost to non-targeted memories
finding: TMR can lower performance on non-targeted memories when the hippocampus is plastic and open to interference. This gives a theory for mixed human results (benefit versus no benefit versus cost).
numbers: Table 1 sign: plastic and noise-driven model shows a negative non-targeted effect; stable models show 0.
limits: Model prediction only. Human evidence for non-targeted cost is mixed.
agent_relevance: Selective rehearsal is zero-sum when capacity is shared. Any agent step that re-reads chosen notes should be checked for harm to the notes it skipped.

source: Barry and Love (2022) A neural network account of memory replay and knowledge consolidation
finding: In a VGG-style network standing in for the ventral visual stream, generative replay (imagined category instances) improved generalisation to new exemplars. Replay from later layers (LOC-like) helped most; earliest layer helped least.
numbers: 10 categories, 10 models, 10 learning episodes. Replay helped newly acquired categories most. A reinforcement-learning chooser that replays categories by their contribution to performance mimicked selective consolidation of weak memories.
limits: Simulation of category learning, not a cue-triggered paradigm. No human data in this paper.
agent_relevance: Replay selection can be learned: pick what to replay by its marginal gain. Gives a principled rule for which notes an agent should re-visit.

source: Sorrenti, Proietto Salanitri, Bellitto et al. (2023) Wake-Sleep Consolidated Learning
finding: A continual-learning method with a wake phase, an NREM phase (replay of stored samples) and a REM phase (dreaming on unrelated data). It beat rehearsal baselines on CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet and FG-ImageNet.
numbers: Table 4 ablation (ER-ACE, Tiny-ImageNet 1/2): wake only 4.70 final avg accuracy; wake+REM 25.68; wake+NREM 27.61; wake+REM+NREM 35.68. Gain over baselines about 2 points (FG-ImageNet) to 12 points (CIFAR-10). Joint upper bound 50.81 on Tiny-ImageNet.
limits: Image classification, small buffers. Replay here is not cue-targeted; stored samples are replayed on a schedule.
agent_relevance: Replay of stored items is most of the effect (4.7 to 27.6); a second pass on unrelated material adds a smaller extra. Supports a cheap rehearsal step in an agent loop.

source: Delanois, Ahuja, Krishnan, Bazhenov (2026) Sleep Replay Consolidation for ANN calibration
finding: A post-training sleep-like phase (spiking, spontaneous replay of internal activity, no labels) changes weights and lowers calibration error without retraining.
numbers: ResNet-152 on CIFAR-100: ECE 0.0622 to 0.0130 with SRC, accuracy 84.9 to 84.8; temperature scaling gave 0.0169. A feed-forward head on ImageNet: ECE 0.0785 to 0.0202, accuracy 76.6 to 75.9. SRC lowered ECE in 5 of 8 models.
limits: Image classifiers only. Effect modest where the head was a single layer. Authors only suggest LLMs as future work.
agent_relevance: Offline replay with no new data can fix overconfidence. For an agent, a quiet pass that re-checks stored confidence is the analogue.

source: Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni (2026) Language Models Need Sleep
finding: A two-stage sleep for LLMs: Knowledge Seeding (distil small model memories into a larger one) then Dreaming (RL-generated synthetic data to rehearse new facts). Reports gains over EWC, in-context learning and SEAL.
numbers: Few-shot ARC protocol on Llama-3.2-1B: Sleep reaches 80% success, above the other methods. SQuAD no-context accuracy and class-incremental text classification (CLINC, Banking, DBpedia) also favour Sleep. Ablation: all components help.
limits: Needs weight updates, so not a scaffold-only method. Self-reported by the authors; small backbone on ARC (11 train, 8 held-out tasks).
agent_relevance: Dreaming is self-generated rehearsal, not cue-targeted. Shows replay of own new knowledge helps a model, but requires training.

source: Lin, Snell, Wang, Packer, Wooders, Stoica, Gonzalez (2025) Sleep-time Compute
finding: Pre-compute inferences about a context while idle, then answer later queries faster. Closest working use of the TMR idea in an LLM loop: guess which queries will come, rehearse them offline.
numbers: About 5x less test-time compute for equal accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME. Scaling sleep-time compute adds up to 13% (GSM-Symbolic) and 18% (AIME). 5 parallel generations beat 10. Accuracy gain grows with how predictable the query is from the context.
limits: o1 showed limited gains. At high test-time budgets standard scaling is better on SWE-Features. Needs predictable queries.
agent_relevance: Direct template for a TMR-like step: rehearse what the memory is likely to be cued for. Use only when the future question is predictable.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: predictability analysis
finding: Examples were binned into five quantiles by how predictable the question is from the context. The gap between sleep-time and plain test-time compute widens with predictability on both P1 and P2.
numbers: Figure 10, GPT-4o-mini, five quantile bins, Stateful GSM-Symbolic P1 and P2. Predictability scored by a language model's log-likelihood of the question given context.
limits: Predictability is measured by one model; only bins are plotted in the text I read.
agent_relevance: This is the machine version of the TMR boundary condition that cues work for memories with a strong cue-target link.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: SWE-Features agent case study
finding: In an agentic coding task the agent explored a repository at sleep-time using related PRs as context. At small budgets this beat standard test-time scaling on F1 of modified files.
numbers: SWE-Features: PRs touching at least 3 files. Figure 11 F1 axis roughly 0.30 to 0.55 over 3000 to 10000 test tokens; sleep-time wins at low budgets, loses at high budgets.
limits: Exact F1 values only read from a plot axis. Single new benchmark by the same authors.
agent_relevance: Offline pre-rehearsal pays at small query budgets; at large budgets it is not worth the cost.

source: Xie (2026) Learning to Forget: SleepGate
finding: A learned sleep micro-cycle on the KV cache evicts or merges superseded entries to cut proactive interference. Biology cited includes selective replay in slow-wave sleep.
numbers: Tiny 4-layer, 793K-parameter transformer, 200 episodes per depth. SleepGate accuracy 99.5% at PI depth 5 and 97.0% at depth 10, then 73.5% at 15, 30.5% at 20, 16.5% at 30. Five baselines (full cache, sliding window, H2O, StreamingLLM, decay only) all at or below 18%.
limits: Toy synthetic benchmark, proof of concept. Collapses at depth 30 with stale retrieval rate 62%. Not tested on real LLMs.
agent_relevance: Targeted forgetting of superseded notes matters as much as targeted strengthening. A scaffold could mark superseded facts rather than only reinforce new ones.

source: Shinde (2026) SCM: Sleep-Consolidated Memory with Algorithmic Forgetting
finding: A memory architecture for chat agents with working memory limit, importance tags, NREM-like consolidation, REM-like dreaming and forgetting.
numbers: 22 recall questions over ten-turn chats: SCM 22/22 (100%) with 24 stored items; FIFO buffer 8/22 (36.4%); vector DB 19/22 (86.4%) with 55 items; no-forget graph 22/22 with 72 items. Noise removal 50/55 (90.9%) after a weight fix; before the fix 0%. Removing NREM step: 20/22.
limits: Single-author research preview, synthetic benchmark of eight tests, tiny sample, self-built tests. A bug fix changed noise removal from 0% to 90.9%, so results are fragile.
agent_relevance: Shows consolidation plus forgetting can shrink memory by two thirds with no recall loss in a toy test; weak evidence.

source: Shin, Kweon, Oh, Lee (2025) Personalized TMR via slow-wave and spindle dynamics
finding: Human TMR study using a machine-style adaptive rule: the number of sleep cue repetitions (1, 2 or 4) was set from each participant's pre-sleep recall difficulty. This beat fixed TMR on hard items.
numbers: 104 word pairs; three groups (personalized TMR, TMR, control), 12 per group; cues in stable NREM. Hardest items (L3): group x time F(2,66)=8.91, p<0.001; improvement only in personalized (t11=-5.68, p<0.001), not TMR (p=0.161) or control (p=0.148); personalized beat TMR t22=3.96 and control t22=4.49 (p<0.001).
limits: N=36 in total, a preprint, word pairs, one lab. Overall main effect of group F(2,66)=5.10, p=0.009 with no interaction in the All condition.
agent_relevance: An adaptive dose rule (rehearse the hard items more) is a design pattern an agent can copy: spend extra re-reads on items it predicts it will get wrong.

source: Shin et al. (2025) Personalized TMR: EEG and classification
finding: Personalized cueing increased slow-wave and spindle synchrony; EEG features correlated with behaviour for challenging memories, and a classifier separated personalized from fixed TMR.
numbers: Difficulty rating correlated strongly negatively with accuracy (rho -0.878 to -0.948). Error-correction ratio (incorrect to correct) higher for personalized TMR than control, p=0.010 (All) and p=0.015 (L3).
limits: Correlational EEG with 12 per group; classification accuracy not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Gives a self-rated difficulty signal that tracked accuracy; an agent could use its own confidence the same way to choose what to rehearse.

source: Esfahani, Daraie, Zerr, Weber, Dresler (2023) Dreamento toolbox
finding: Open-source Python tool that records a wearable EEG headband, scores sleep stage in real time and triggers visual, auditory or tactile cues. Built for lucid-dream work and says it also fits closed-loop auditory stimulation and TMR.
numbers: Real-time autoscoring uses a CNN plus LSTM; offline mode uses a heavier scorer. No TMR memory results are reported in this paper.
limits: Software description only; scoring accuracy numbers were not extracted from the pages I read.
agent_relevance: Machine side of TMR: a stage classifier gates when cues play. Matches the idea that cues must be gated by state; an agent needs a state check before replay.

source: Rasch, Buchel, Gais, Born (2007) Odor cues during slow-wave sleep prompt declarative memory consolidation
finding: Founding study: an odour present during card-pair learning and again in slow-wave sleep improved next-day recall; the same odour in REM or wake did not. Not opened this session.
numbers: Not verified here.
limits: Odour re-exposure effect not verified by me; N small.
agent_relevance: Cue must match a context tied to the memory and arrive in the right sleep state.

source: Hu, Cheng, Tang et al. (2020) Promoting memory consolidation during sleep: meta-analysis of TMR
finding: Meta-analysis of cueing studies reports a small positive overall effect. Not opened this session.
numbers: Pooled effect size not verified here.
limits: Number not verified.
agent_relevance: Sets the expected size of a cue effect: small and variable.

source: Cairney et al. (2016) TMR benefits depend on memory accuracy and direct cue-memory links (search snippet)
finding: Search snippet: TMR benefits depended on memory accuracy and direct cue-memory associations. Not opened.
numbers: None extracted.
limits: A PMC fetch hit a verification screen, so this entry relies on the search snippet only.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: cueing helps memories that are already partly learned.

source: Emergent Mind summary of Sleep-time Compute (2025)
finding: Secondary summary says at very high test-time budgets the baseline sometimes slightly beats sleep-time compute. This is consistent with the opened paper's SWE-Features figure.
numbers: Not separately quantified.
limits: Secondary source only.
agent_relevance: Same limit: gain at low budgets only.

source: Gap note: LLM TMR search 2020-2026 (arXiv, web search)
finding: No paper found that gives an LLM an externally supplied cue to bias its own replay or rehearsal and then measures recall. arXiv exact-phrase search returned only two papers (personalized TMR, Dreamento). Web search found only the CLS TMR model.
numbers: Two exact-phrase arXiv hits; one web search for TMR plus neural network or language model returned no machine TMR study beyond Lu et al. 2024 and Barry and Love 2022.
limits: Absence of results in a few searches under a rate limit; Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned rate-limit errors, so coverage is incomplete.
agent_relevance: The scaffold step 'cue a stored note during an idle pass' is untested; any claim for it would be new.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) PI-LLM proactive interference (as described by Xie 2026)
finding: Described in the SleepGate paper: stale key-value updates drive retrieval accuracy log-linearly toward zero, and prompts telling the model to ignore old values give only marginal relief.
numbers: As relayed: accuracy falls log-linearly with number of superseded values. Xie reports full-cache accuracy 8.0% at depth 1 in his small model.
limits: Second-hand description; original not opened.
agent_relevance: Shows a failure that a rehearsal or cue step must not worsen: old values compete with new ones.

source: Xie (2026) SleepGate: ablation and compute cost
finding: A decay-only version without learned gating performs no better than other baselines, so a plain forgetting rule is not enough. Sleep overhead is a measurable cost.
numbers: Decay-only 12.5% at depth 2; sleep overhead 15.6%; best baseline StreamingLLM 18.0% at n=2; SleepGate 99.0%.
limits: Same toy setting as above.
agent_relevance: Costs about a sixth in compute; a selective, learned choice of what to keep beats a blunt rule.

source: Shinde (2026) SCM ablation of consolidation phases
finding: Ablation table: removing the value tagger drops recall to 18/22 (81.8%) and removing NREM consolidation drops it to 20/22 (90.9%). Removing REM dreaming, forgetting or self-model leaves recall at 22/22.
numbers: Store sizes: full 24; no working-memory limit 89; no forgetting 72.
limits: Tiny benchmark; 22 questions, so one question is 4.5 points.
agent_relevance: Importance tagging and a replay-like consolidation step are what protect recall; the dream step did nothing for recall here.

source: Sorrenti et al. (2023) WSCL: efficiency
finding: The wake-sleep scheme also cut the number of parameter updates by roughly 2 to 17% depending on setting.
numbers: About 17.14% fewer updates in one setting; 2% to 17% overall.
limits: Image tasks only.
agent_relevance: Offline rehearsal can lower total effort, not just raise accuracy.

source: Delanois et al. (2026) SRC: complementarity with temperature scaling
finding: Sleep replay and temperature scaling were complementary; combining them gave the best Brier score and entropy trade-off for AlexNet and VGG19 according to the authors.
numbers: ResNet-152 CIFAR-100: ECE after SRC+TS 0.0142 versus SRC alone 0.0130 versus TS alone 0.0169. NLL 0.570 (SRC), 0.563 (TS).
limits: On this model SRC alone had lower ECE than the combination; the combined benefit is metric-dependent.
agent_relevance: Combine a cheap output-level fix with an offline pass, and measure several metrics.
